Instructions: Gegeben ist eine interne Tabelle mit Produkt-IDs. Generieren Sie für jede ID einen Barcode und speichern Sie das Ergebnis (ID und Barcode XSTRING) in einer neuen internen Tabelle. Fehler bei der Generierung sollen abgefangen und protokolliert werden.
hint: Nutzen Sie eine `FOR`-Expression, um die interne Tabelle zu verarbeiten, und `TRY...CATCH` innerhalb der Schleife.
solution:
CLASS zcl_barcode_multi_gen DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_product_barcode,
             product_id    TYPE string,
             barcode_xstring TYPE xstring,
             error_message   TYPE string,
           END OF ty_product_barcode.
    TYPES tt_product_barcode TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_product_barcode WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS generate_barcodes_for_products
      IMPORTING
        it_product_ids TYPE string_table
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_results) TYPE tt_product_barcode.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_barcode_multi_gen IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD generate_barcodes_for_products.
    DATA(lv_barcode_type) = 'CODE128'.
    DATA(lv_width) = 200.
    DATA(lv_height) = 100.

    rt_results = VALUE #( FOR product_id IN it_product_ids
                           LET ls_result = VALUE ty_product_barcode( product_id = product_id )
                           IN
                             TRY.
                                 ls_result-barcode_xstring = cl_rstx_barcode_renderer=>create_barcode_bmp_xstring(
                                   i_barcode_type = lv_barcode_type
                                   i_barcode_data = product_id
                                   i_width        = lv_width
                                   i_height       = lv_height
                                 ).
                               CATCH cx_rstx_barcode_error INTO DATA(lx_barcode_error).
                                 ls_result-error_message = |Fehler für { product_id }: { lx_barcode_error->get_text( ) }|.
                             ENDTRY.
                             ( ls_result ) ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_multiple_barcodes.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_barcode_multi_gen( ).
    DATA(lt_product_ids) = VALUE string_table( ( 'PROD1' ) ( 'PROD2' ) ( 'INVALID_LONG_PRODUCT_ID_THAT_WILL_FAIL' ) ).
    DATA(lt_results) = lo_cut->generate_barcodes_for_products( lt_product_ids ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lines( lt_results ) exp = 3 msg = 'Expected 3 results' ).

    READ TABLE lt_results INTO DATA(ls_result_prod1) WITH KEY product_id = 'PROD1'.
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_not_initial( act = ls_result_prod1-barcode_xstring msg = 'Barcode for PROD1 should be generated' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial( act = ls_result_prod1-error_message msg = 'No error for PROD1' ).

    READ TABLE lt_results INTO DATA(ls_result_invalid) WITH KEY product_id = 'INVALID_LONG_PRODUCT_ID_THAT_WILL_FAIL'.
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial( act = ls_result_invalid-barcode_xstring msg = 'Barcode for invalid ID should not be generated' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_not_initial( act = ls_result_invalid-error_message msg = 'Error message for invalid ID expected' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_contains( act = ls_result_invalid-error_message exp = 'Fehler' msg = 'Error message should contain expected text' ).
  ENDMETHOD.

explanation: Dieses Beispiel nutzt eine `FOR`-Expression, um eine interne Tabelle zu iterieren und für jedes Element einen Barcode zu generieren. Die `LET`-Anweisung ermöglicht die Deklaration lokaler Variablen innerhalb der Expression. `TRY...CATCH` wird pro Element verwendet, um individuelle Fehler abzufangen und zu protokollieren, ohne den gesamten Prozess zu unterbrechen. Dies ist ein sehr funktionaler und effizienter Ansatz zur Verarbeitung von Tabellen.
keywords: Internal Tables, FOR Expression, TRY...CATCH, Functional Programming, Barcode, XSTRING

Instructions: Definieren Sie eine benutzerdefinierte Ausnahme-Klasse für Barcode-Fehler und verwenden Sie diese, um spezifische Fehler bei der Barcode-Generierung zu signalisieren und abzufangen.
hint: Erstellen Sie eine Klasse, die von `cx_static_check` erbt, und verwenden Sie `RAISE EXCEPTION TYPE`.
solution:
CLASS zcx_barcode_error DEFINITION PUBLIC INHERITING FROM cx_static_check.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES if_abap_behv_message.
    CONSTANTS: BEGIN OF barcode_generation_failed,
                 msgid TYPE symsgid VALUE 'ZMSG_BARCODE',
                 msgno TYPE symsgno VALUE '001',
                 attr1 TYPE scx_attrname VALUE 'PREVIOUS',
                 attr2 TYPE scx_attrname VALUE '',
                 attr3 TYPE scx_attrname VALUE '',
                 attr4 TYPE scx_attrname VALUE '',
               END OF barcode_generation_failed.

    METHODS constructor
      IMPORTING
        textid   LIKE if_t100_message=>t100key OPTIONAL
        previous LIKE previous OPTIONAL.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcx_barcode_error IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
    CALL METHOD super->constructor
      EXPORTING

Instructions: Generieren Sie einen Barcode nur, wenn die Eingabedaten eine bestimmte Länge nicht überschreiten. Andernfalls geben Sie einen leeren XSTRING und eine Fehlermeldung zurück. Fangen Sie auch interne Barcode-Fehler ab.
hint: Verwenden Sie eine `COND`-Expression oder `IF` für die Längenprüfung und `TRY...CATCH` für die Barcode-Generierung.
solution:
CLASS zcl_barcode_cond_gen DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_barcode_output,
             barcode_xstring TYPE xstring,
             error_message   TYPE string,
           END OF ty_barcode_output.

    METHODS generate_conditional_barcode
      IMPORTING
        iv_data TYPE string
        iv_max_length TYPE i DEFAULT 20
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rs_output) TYPE ty_barcode_output.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_barcode_cond_gen IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD generate_conditional_barcode.
    DATA(lv_barcode_type) = 'CODE128'.
    DATA(lv_width) = 200.
    DATA(lv_height) = 100.

    rs_output = COND #( WHEN strlen( iv_data ) > iv_max_length
                        THEN VALUE ty_barcode_output( error_message = |Eingabedaten '{ iv_data }' überschreiten maximale Länge von { iv_max_length } Zeichen.| )
                        ELSE
                          TRY.
                              VALUE ty_barcode_output(
                                barcode_xstring = cl_rstx_barcode_renderer=>create_barcode_bmp_xstring(
                                  i_barcode_type = lv_barcode_type
                                  i_barcode_data = iv_data
                                  i_width        = lv_width
                                  i_height       = lv_height
                                )
                              )
                            CATCH cx_rstx_barcode_error INTO DATA(lx_barcode_error).
                              VALUE ty_barcode_output(
                                error_message = |Barcode-Generierung fehlgeschlagen für '{ iv_data }': { lx_barcode_error->get_text( ) }|
                              )
                          ENDTRY
                      ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

Instructions: Filtern Sie eine Liste von Produkt-IDs, um nur gültige IDs (z.B. nicht leer und unter einer bestimmten Länge) für die Barcode-Generierung zu berücksichtigen. Generieren Sie dann Barcodes für die gefilterten IDs und sammeln Sie die Ergebnisse (erfolgreich generierte Barcodes und Fehler).
hint: Verwenden Sie `FILTER` für die Vorverarbeitung der Daten und eine `FOR`-Expression mit `TRY...CATCH` für die Generierung.
solution:
CLASS zcl_barcode_filter_gen DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_barcode_result,
             product_id    TYPE string,
             barcode_xstring TYPE xstring,
             error_message   TYPE string,
           END OF ty_barcode_result.
    TYPES tt_barcode_results TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_barcode_result WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS generate_filtered_barcodes
      IMPORTING
        it_product_ids TYPE string_table
        iv_max_len     TYPE i DEFAULT 20
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_results) TYPE tt_barcode_results.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_barcode_filter_gen IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD generate_filtered_barcodes.
    DATA(lv_barcode_type) = 'CODE128'.
    DATA(lv_width) = 200.
    DATA(lv_height) = 100.

    DATA(lt_valid_ids) = FILTER string_table FROM it_product_ids
                                 WHERE table_line IS NOT INITIAL
                                 AND   strlen( table_line ) <= iv_max_len.

    rt_results = VALUE #( FOR product_id IN lt_valid_ids
                           LET ls_result = VALUE ty_barcode_result( product_id = product_id )
                           IN
                             TRY.
                                 ls_result-barcode_xstring = cl_rstx_barcode_renderer=>create_barcode_bmp_xstring(
                                   i_barcode_type = lv_barcode_type
                                   i_barcode_data = product_id
                                   i_width        = lv_width
                                   i_height       = lv_height
                                 ).
                               CATCH cx_rstx_barcode_error INTO DATA(lx_barcode_error).
                                 ls_result-error_message = |Fehler für { product_id }: { lx_barcode_error->get_text( ) }|.
                             ENDTRY.
                             ( ls_result ) ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

Instructions: Aggregieren Sie den Erfolg oder Misserfolg der Barcode-Generierung für eine Liste von Daten in einem einzigen Status-Objekt. Verwenden Sie `REDUCE`.
hint: Nutzen Sie die `REDUCE`-Expression, um über die Daten zu iterieren und einen aggregierten Status zu erstellen, wobei `TRY...CATCH` für jeden Schritt verwendet wird.
solution:
CLASS zcl_barcode_reduce_status DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_aggregated_status,
             total_items     TYPE i,
             successful_items TYPE i,
             failed_items    TYPE i,
             error_messages  TYPE string_table,
           END OF ty_aggregated_status.

    METHODS aggregate_barcode_status
      IMPORTING
        it_data TYPE string_table
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rs_status) TYPE ty_aggregated_status.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_barcode_reduce_status IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD aggregate_barcode_status.
    DATA(lv_barcode_type) = 'CODE128'.
    DATA(lv_width) = 200.
    DATA(lv_height) = 100.

    rs_status = REDUCE ty_aggregated_status(
      INIT result = VALUE ty_aggregated_status( )
      FOR data_item IN it_data
      NEXT
        result-total_items = result-total_items + 1
        TRY.
            cl_rstx_barcode_renderer=>create_barcode_bmp_xstring(
              i_barcode_type = lv_barcode_type
              i_barcode_data = data_item
              i_width        = lv_width
              i_height       = lv_height
            ).
            result-successful_items = result-successful_items + 1
          CATCH cx_rstx_barcode_error INTO DATA(lx_barcode_error).
            result-failed_items = result-failed_items + 1.
            APPEND |Fehler für '{ data_item }': { lx_barcode_error->get_text( ) }| TO result-error_messages.
        ENDTRY
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.

  METHOD test_aggregate_status.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_barcode_reduce_status( ).
    DATA(lt_input_data) = VALUE string_table( ( 'ITEM1' ) ( 'ITEM2' ) ( 'INVALID_LONG_ITEM_THAT_WILL_FAIL' ) ( 'ITEM3' ) ( 'ANOTHER_INVALID_ITEM_FOR_FAILURE' ) ).
    DATA(ls_status) = lo_cut->aggregate_barcode_status( lt_input_data ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = ls_status-total_items exp = 5 msg = 'Expected 5 total items' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = ls_status-successful_items exp = 3 msg = 'Expected 3 successful items' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = ls_status-failed_items exp = 2 msg = 'Expected 2 failed items' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lines( ls_status-error_messages ) exp = 2 msg = 'Expected 2 error messages' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_contains( act = ls_status-error_messages[1] exp = 'Fehler' msg = 'First error message should contain "Fehler"' ).
  ENDMETHOD.

explanation: Die `REDUCE`-Expression ist ein mächtiges Werkzeug für die funktionale Programmierung in ABAP, um eine Liste von Werten zu einem einzelnen Ergebnis zu aggregieren. In diesem Beispiel wird sie verwendet, um den Status der Barcode-Generierung für mehrere Elemente zu sammeln. `TRY...CATCH` innerhalb der `REDUCE`-Expression ermöglicht es, Fehler pro Element zu behandeln und die aggregierten Zähler und Fehlermeldungen entsprechend zu aktualisieren. Dies ist eine sehr effiziente und ausdrucksstarke Art der Datenaggregation.
keywords: Functional Programming, REDUCE Expression, Internal Tables, TRY...CATCH, Aggregation, Barcode

        " CONCEPT: In a real scenario, you would store this XSTRING
        " in a custom transparent table or a temporary LOB storage.
        " Direct write to STXD_STXFTXT is not standard practice.

        IF lv_barcode_xstring IS NOT INITIAL.

hint: Verwenden Sie `cl_rstx_barcode_renderer` und `cl_http_utility=>encode_x_base64` sowie `TRY...CATCH`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_barcode_base64 DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS generate_barcode_base64
      IMPORTING
        iv_data TYPE string
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_base64_string) TYPE string
      RAISING
        zcx_barcode_error.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_barcode_base64 IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD generate_barcode_base64.
    DATA(lv_barcode_type) = 'CODE128'.
    DATA(lv_width) = 200.
    DATA(lv_height) = 100.
    DATA(lv_barcode_xstring) TYPE xstring.

    TRY.
        lv_barcode_xstring = cl_rstx_barcode_renderer=>create_barcode_bmp_xstring(
          i_barcode_type = lv_barcode_type
          i_barcode_data = iv_data
          i_width        = lv_width
          i_height       = lv_height
        ).

        rv_base64_string = cl_http_utility=>encode_x_base64( lv_barcode_xstring ).

      CATCH cx_rstx_barcode_error INTO DATA(lx_barcode_error).
        RAISE EXCEPTION TYPE zcx_barcode_error
          EXPORTING
            textid = zcx_barcode_error=>barcode_generation_failed
            previous = lx_barcode_error.
    ENDTRY.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_base64_success FOR TESTING RAISING zcx_barcode_error.
    METHODS test_base64_failure FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_base64_success.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_barcode_base64( ).
    DATA(lv_base64) = lo_cut->generate_barcode_base64( 'BASE64_TEST' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_not_initial( act = lv_base64 msg = 'Base64 string should not be initial' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_not_equals( act = lv_base64 exp = 'BASE64_TEST' msg = 'Base64 string should be encoded' ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_base64_failure.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_barcode_base64( ).
    TRY.
        lo_cut->generate_barcode_base64( 'TooLongInvalidDataForBarcodeGenerationWhichWillFail' ).
        cl_abap_unit_assert=>fail( msg = 'Expected exception zcx_barcode_error was not raised' ).
      CATCH zcx_barcode_error.
        cl_abap_unit_assert=>pass( msg = 'Expected exception zcx_barcode_error caught' ).
    ENDTRY.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Dieses Beispiel zeigt die Umwandlung eines generierten Barcode-XSTRING in einen Base64-kodierten String mithilfe von `cl_http_utility=>encode_x_base64`. Dies ist nützlich, um Barcodes direkt in Webseiten (z.B. als `data:image/bmp;base64,...`) oder andere Textformate einzubetten. Die Fehlerbehandlung mit `TRY...CATCH` stellt sicher, dass Probleme bei der Barcode-Generierung korrekt abgefangen werden.
keywords: Barcode, Base64, XSTRING, Graphics, Web Integration, TRY...CATCH

Instructions: Aktualisieren Sie den Preis eines Fluges in der Tabelle `SFLIGHT` für eine bestimmte Fluggesellschaft, Flugnummer und Datum.
hint: Verwenden Sie die `UPDATE` Anweisung mit `SET` und `WHERE` Klauseln.
solution:
CLASS zcl_sflight_updater DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS update_flight_price
      IMPORTING
        iv_carrid   TYPE sflight-carrid
        iv_connid   TYPE sflight-connid
        iv_fldate   TYPE sflight-fldate
        iv_new_price TYPE sflight-price
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_success) TYPE abap_bool.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_sflight_updater IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD update_flight_price.
    UPDATE sflight SET price = iv_new_price
      WHERE carrid = iv_carrid
        AND connid = iv_connid
        AND fldate = iv_fldate.
    rv_success = COND #( WHEN sy-dbcnt = 1 THEN abap_true ELSE abap_false ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.

    DELETE FROM sflight WHERE carrid = 'LH' AND connid = '0400' AND fldate = '20251201'.

Instructions: Aktualisieren Sie die Preise mehrerer Flüge in der Tabelle `SFLIGHT` basierend auf einer internen Tabelle von Flugdaten.
hint: Verwenden Sie `UPDATE sflight FROM TABLE @it_flight_updates`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_sflight_mass_updater DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_flight_update,
             carrid   TYPE sflight-carrid,
             connid   TYPE sflight-connid,
             fldate   TYPE sflight-fldate,
             price    TYPE sflight-price,
           END OF ty_flight_update.
    TYPES: tt_flight_update TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_flight_update WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS update_flights_from_table
      IMPORTING
        it_flight_updates TYPE tt_flight_update
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_updated_count) TYPE i.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_sflight_mass_updater IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD update_flights_from_table.
    UPDATE sflight FROM TABLE @it_flight_updates.
    rv_updated_count = sy-dbcnt.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS setup FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_mass_update FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_no_update FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD setup.
    " Ensure test records exist
    DELETE FROM sflight WHERE carrid = 'LH' AND connid IN ('0400', '0500') AND fldate = '20251202'.
    INSERT sflight FROM TABLE @( VALUE #( 
      ( carrid = 'LH' connid = '0400' fldate = '20251202' price = 100.00 currency = 'EUR' planetype = 'A320' seatsmax = 100 seatsocc = 50 )
      ( carrid = 'LH' connid = '0500' fldate = '20251202' price = 200.00 currency = 'EUR' planetype = 'A320' seatsmax = 100 seatsocc = 50 )
    ) ).
    COMMIT WORK.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_mass_update.
    DATA(lo_updater) = NEW zcl_sflight_mass_updater( ).
    DATA(lt_updates) = VALUE zcl_sflight_mass_updater=>tt_flight_update(
      ( carrid = 'LH' connid = '0400' fldate = '20251202' price = 120.00 )
      ( carrid = 'LH' connid = '0500' fldate = '20251202' price = 220.00 )
      ( carrid = 'XX' connid = '9999' fldate = '20251202' price = 300.00 ) " Non-existent
    ).
    DATA(lv_updated_count) = lo_updater->update_flights_from_table( it_flight_updates = lt_updates ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_updated_count exp = 2 ).

    " Verify updates
    SELECT carrid, connid, price FROM sflight INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_prices)
      WHERE carrid = 'LH' AND connid IN ('0400', '0500') AND fldate = '20251202' ORDER BY connid.

    READ TABLE lt_prices INTO DATA(ls_flight1) INDEX 1.
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = ls_flight1-price exp = 120.00 ).

    READ TABLE lt_prices INTO DATA(ls_flight2) INDEX 2.
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = ls_flight2-price exp = 220.00 ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_no_update.
    DATA(lo_updater) = NEW zcl_sflight_mass_updater( ).
    DATA(lt_updates) = VALUE zcl_sflight_mass_updater=>tt_flight_update(
      ( carrid = 'XX' connid = '9999' fldate = '20251202' price = 300.00 )
    ).
    DATA(lv_updated_count) = lo_updater->update_flights_from_table( it_flight_updates = lt_updates ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_updated_count exp = 0 ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Die `UPDATE FROM TABLE` Anweisung ist die effizienteste Methode, um mehrere Datensätze auf einmal zu aktualisieren, da sie die Datenbankzugriffe minimiert. Die Verwendung von `VALUE #(...)` für die Initialisierung interner Tabellen ist ein modernes Sprachmerkmal.
keywords: UPDATE, FROM TABLE, Database, Mass Update, VALUE

Instructions: Aktualisieren Sie den Preis von Flügen in `SFLIGHT` basierend auf einer Bedingung: Erhöhen Sie den Preis um 10%, wenn der aktuelle Preis unter 100 EUR liegt, sonst um 5%.
hint: Verwenden Sie eine `CASE` Expression direkt in der `SET` Klausel der `UPDATE` Anweisung.
solution:
CLASS zcl_sflight_cond_updater DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS update_prices_conditionally
      IMPORTING
        iv_carrid TYPE sflight-carrid
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_updated_count) TYPE i.

CLASS zcl_sflight_cond_updater IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD update_prices_conditionally.

              END
      WHERE carrid = iv_carrid.
    rv_updated_count = sy-dbcnt.
  ENDMETHOD.

Instructions: Vergleichen Sie zwei Strings sprachsensitiv, um die korrekte Sortierreihenfolge für eine bestimmte Sprache zu ermitteln.
hint: Verwenden Sie `cl_i18n_utils=>get_collator` und `compare_strings`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_i18n_string_compare DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS compare_strings_by_locale
      IMPORTING
        iv_string1  TYPE string
        iv_string2  TYPE string
        iv_language TYPE sy-langu OPTIONAL
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_comparison_result) TYPE i. " -1: s1 < s2, 0: s1 = s2, 1: s1 > s2
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_i18n_string_compare IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD compare_strings_by_locale.
    DATA(lv_language) = COND #( WHEN iv_language IS SUPPLIED THEN iv_language ELSE sy-langu ).
    DATA(lo_collator) = cl_i18n_utils=>get_collator( iv_language = lv_language ).
    rv_comparison_result = lo_collator->compare_strings( iv_string1 = iv_string1, iv_string2 = iv_string2 ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_compare_german FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_compare_swedish FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_compare_german.
    DATA(lo_comparer) = NEW zcl_i18n_string_compare( ).
    " In German, 'ä' sorts like 'a' or 'ae'
    DATA(lv_result) = lo_comparer->compare_strings_by_locale( iv_string1 = 'Müller', iv_string2 = 'Muster', iv_language = 'D' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_result exp = 1 ). " Müller > Muster

    lv_result = lo_comparer->compare_strings_by_locale( iv_string1 = 'Muster', iv_string2 = 'Müller', iv_language = 'D' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_result exp = -1 ). " Muster < Müller
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_compare_swedish.
    DATA(lo_comparer) = NEW zcl_i18n_string_compare( ).
    " In Swedish, 'å' comes after 'z'
    DATA(lv_result) = lo_comparer->compare_strings_by_locale( iv_string1 = 'Zebra', iv_string2 = 'Åland', iv_language = 'S' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_result exp = -1 ). " Zebra < Åland

    lv_result = lo_comparer->compare_strings_by_locale( iv_string1 = 'Åland', iv_string2 = 'Zebra', iv_language = 'S' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_result exp = 1 ). " Åland > Zebra
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Die sprachsensitive String-Sortierung ist komplex und kann nicht einfach mit Standard-ABAP-Vergleichen gelöst werden. `cl_i18n_utils=>get_collator` bietet eine robuste Lösung, die die spezifischen Sortierregeln jeder Sprache berücksichtigt, was für internationale Anwendungen unerlässlich ist.
keywords: cl_i18n_utils, String Comparison, Collation, Internationalization, Sort

CLASS zcl_sflight_seats_updater DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.

CLASS zcl_sflight_seats_updater IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD update_seats_occupied.
    UPDATE sflight SET
      seatsocc = LEAST( seatsocc + iv_increase, seatsmax )

ENDCLASS.

Instructions: Aktualisieren Sie den `CURRENCY` Code für alle Flüge einer bestimmten Fluggesellschaft in `SFLIGHT` auf einen neuen Wert, aber nur, wenn der `PRICE` über einem bestimmten Schwellenwert liegt. Verwenden Sie eine interne Tabelle für die zu aktualisierenden Flüge.
hint: Verwenden Sie `UPDATE FROM TABLE` in Kombination mit einem `FOR` Ausdruck, um die interne Tabelle vorzubereiten.
solution:
CLASS zcl_sflight_currency_updater DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_flight_key_price,
             carrid   TYPE sflight-carrid,
             connid   TYPE sflight-connid,
             fldate   TYPE sflight-fldate,
             price    TYPE sflight-price,
           END OF ty_flight_key_price.
    TYPES: tt_flight_key_price TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_flight_key_price WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS update_currency_conditionally
      IMPORTING
        iv_carrid      TYPE sflight-carrid
        iv_price_threshold TYPE sflight-price
        iv_new_currency  TYPE sflight-currency
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_updated_count) TYPE i.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_sflight_currency_updater IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD update_currency_conditionally.
    DATA lt_flights_to_update TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF sflight WITH EMPTY KEY.

    SELECT carrid, connid, fldate, price, currency
      FROM sflight INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_all_flights)
      WHERE carrid = iv_carrid AND price > iv_price_threshold.

    lt_flights_to_update = VALUE #( FOR ls_flight IN lt_all_flights
                                     ( carrid = ls_flight-carrid
                                       connid = ls_flight-connid
                                       fldate = ls_flight-fldate
                                       currency = iv_new_currency ) ).

    UPDATE sflight FROM TABLE @lt_flights_to_update.
    rv_updated_count = sy-dbcnt.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS setup FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_update_currency_success FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_update_currency_no_match FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD setup.
    DELETE FROM sflight WHERE carrid = 'BA' AND fldate = '20251207'.
    INSERT sflight FROM TABLE @( VALUE #( 
      ( carrid = 'BA' connid = '0010' fldate = '20251207' price = 150.00 currency = 'GBP' planetype = 'A320' seatsmax = 100 seatsocc = 50 )
      ( carrid = 'BA' connid = '0020' fldate = '20251207' price = 80.00 currency = 'GBP' planetype = 'B737' seatsmax = 80 seatsocc = 40 )
      ( carrid = 'BA' connid = '0030' fldate = '20251207' price = 250.00 currency = 'GBP' planetype = 'A380' seatsmax = 400 seatsocc = 200 )
    ) ).
    COMMIT WORK.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_update_currency_success.
    DATA(lo_updater) = NEW zcl_sflight_currency_updater( ).
    DATA(lv_updated) = lo_updater->update_currency_conditionally(
      iv_carrid = 'BA'
      iv_price_threshold = 100.00
      iv_new_currency = 'EUR'
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_updated exp = 2 ).

    SELECT connid, currency FROM sflight INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_currency_results)
      WHERE carrid = 'BA' AND fldate = '20251207' ORDER BY connid.

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_currency_results[ 1 ]-currency exp = 'EUR' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_currency_results[ 2 ]-currency exp = 'GBP' ). " Price 80 < 100
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_currency_results[ 3 ]-currency exp = 'EUR' ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_update_currency_no_match.
    DATA(lo_updater) = NEW zcl_sflight_currency_updater( ).

explanation: Dieses Beispiel kombiniert modernes Open SQL (`SELECT INTO TABLE @DATA(...)`) mit einem `FOR` Ausdruck, um eine interne Tabelle für die `UPDATE FROM TABLE` Anweisung vorzubereiten. Dies ist eine sehr effiziente Methode, um bedingte Massenaktualisierungen durchzuführen, da die Daten nur einmal von der Datenbank gelesen und dann in einem einzigen Datenbankaufruf aktualisiert werden.
keywords: UPDATE, FROM TABLE, FOR, Database, Conditional Update, Internal Tables

explanation: Dieses Beispiel zeigt das Factory Method Pattern. Eine abstrakte Creator-Klasse deklariert eine Fabrikmethode, die ein abstraktes Produkt zurückgibt. Konkrete Creator-Klassen überschreiben diese Methode, um spezifische konkrete Produkte zu erzeugen. Dies entkoppelt die Objekterzeugung von der Verwendung.
keywords: ABSTRACT CLASS, FACTORY METHOD, Design Patterns, INTERFACE

Instructions: Implementieren Sie das Strategy Pattern, wobei die Strategie durch ein Interface definiert wird und konkrete Strategien dieses Interface implementieren. Ein Kontext verwendet die Strategie.
hint: Nutzen Sie `INTERFACE` für die Strategie und Dependency Injection im Kontext.
solution:
INTERFACE zif_abs_strategy.
  METHODS execute_strategy IMPORTING iv_input TYPE i RETURNING VALUE(rv_result) TYPE i.
ENDINTERFACE.

CLASS zcl_abs_context DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS: constructor IMPORTING io_strategy TYPE REF TO zif_abs_strategy,
             perform_operation IMPORTING iv_input TYPE i RETURNING VALUE(rv_result) TYPE i.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA mo_strategy TYPE REF TO zif_abs_strategy.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_abs_context IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
    mo_strategy = io_strategy.
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD perform_operation.
    rv_result = mo_strategy->execute_strategy( iv_input ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_abs_strategy_add DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES zif_abs_strategy.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_abs_strategy_add IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD zif_abs_strategy~execute_strategy.
    rv_result = iv_input + 10.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_abs_strategy_multiply DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES zif_abs_strategy.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_abs_strategy_multiply IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD zif_abs_strategy~execute_strategy.
    rv_result = iv_input * 2.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_strategy_add FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_strategy_multiply FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_strategy_add.
    DATA(lo_strategy_add) = NEW zcl_abs_strategy_add( ).
    DATA(lo_context) = NEW zcl_abs_context( lo_strategy_add ).
    DATA(lv_result) = lo_context->perform_operation( 5 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lv_result,

      msg = 'Add strategy failed.'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD test_strategy_multiply.
    DATA(lo_strategy_multiply) = NEW zcl_abs_strategy_multiply( ).
    DATA(lo_context) = NEW zcl_abs_context( lo_strategy_multiply ).
    DATA(lv_result) = lo_context->perform_operation( 5 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lv_result,
      exp = 10,
      msg = 'Multiply strategy failed.'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Das Strategy Pattern ermöglicht es, Algorithmen zur Laufzeit auszutauschen. Hier wird ein Interface für die Strategie verwendet, das von konkreten Strategieklassen implementiert wird. Der Kontext erhält die Strategie per Dependency Injection, was Flexibilität und Testbarkeit erhöht.
keywords: INTERFACE, Strategy Pattern, Polymorphism, Dependency Injection

Instructions: Erstellen Sie eine abstrakte Basisklasse mit einer statischen Fabrikmethode, die Instanzen von konkreten Unterklassen basierend auf einem Typ-Parameter erzeugt.
hint: Nutzen Sie `ABSTRACT CLASS`, `STATIC METHOD` und `CASE` für die Objekterzeugung.

CLASS zcl_abs_shape DEFINITION PUBLIC ABSTRACT FINAL.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS get_area ABSTRACT RETURNING VALUE(rv_area) TYPE decfloat16.
    CLASS METHODS create_shape
      IMPORTING iv_type TYPE string
      RETURNING VALUE(ro_shape) TYPE REF TO zcl_abs_shape.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_abs_shape IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD create_shape.
    CASE iv_type.
      WHEN 'CIRCLE'.
        ro_shape = NEW zcl_abs_circle( ).
      WHEN 'SQUARE'.
        ro_shape = NEW zcl_abs_square( ).
      WHEN OTHERS.
        " Optional: Raise exception for unknown type
    ENDCASE.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_abs_circle DEFINITION INHERITING FROM zcl_abs_shape FINAL.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS constructor IMPORTING iv_radius TYPE decfloat16.
    METHODS get_area REDEFINITION.
  PRIVATE SECTION.

ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_abs_circle IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
    mv_radius = iv_radius.
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD get_area.
    rv_area = mv_radius * mv_radius * '3.14159'.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_abs_square DEFINITION INHERITING FROM zcl_abs_shape FINAL.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS constructor IMPORTING iv_side TYPE decfloat16.
    METHODS get_area REDEFINITION.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA mv_side TYPE decfloat16.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_abs_square IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
    mv_side = iv_side.
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD get_area.
    rv_area = mv_side * mv_side.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

explanation: Eine statische Fabrikmethode in einer abstrakten Basisklasse ermöglicht die zentrale Erzeugung von Objekten aus einer Hierarchie von Unterklassen. Dies verbirgt die konkrete Implementierung der Objekterzeugung vor dem Client-Code und erleichtert die Erweiterbarkeit.
keywords: ABSTRACT CLASS, STATIC METHOD, Factory, Polymorphism

Instructions: Definieren Sie eine abstrakte Basisklasse für Event-Handler, die eine abstrakte Methode zur Verarbeitung eines generischen Events enthält. Implementieren Sie einen konkreten Handler und einen Event-Raiser.
hint: Nutzen Sie `ABSTRACT CLASS`, `ABSTRACT METHOD` und `EVENTS`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_abs_event_data DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    DATA mv_message TYPE string.
    METHODS constructor IMPORTING iv_message TYPE string.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_abs_event_data IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
    mv_message = iv_message.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_abs_event_handler DEFINITION PUBLIC ABSTRACT FINAL.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS handle_event ABSTRACT FOR EVENT event_triggered OF zcl_abs_event_raiser.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_abs_event_raiser DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    EVENTS event_triggered EXPORTING VALUE(eo_data) TYPE REF TO zcl_abs_event_data.
    METHODS raise_event IMPORTING iv_message TYPE string.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_abs_event_raiser IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD raise_event.
    DATA(lo_event_data) = NEW zcl_abs_event_data( iv_message ).
    RAISE EVENT event_triggered EXPORTING eo_data = lo_event_data.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_abs_concrete_handler DEFINITION INHERITING FROM zcl_abs_event_handler FINAL.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    DATA mv_processed_message TYPE string.
    METHODS handle_event REDEFINITION.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_abs_concrete_handler IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD handle_event.
    mv_processed_message = eo_data->mv_message && ' - Processed'.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_event_handling FOR TESTING.

  METHOD test_event_handling.
    DATA(lo_raiser) = NEW zcl_abs_event_raiser( ).
    DATA(lo_handler) = NEW zcl_abs_concrete_handler( ).
    SET HANDLER lo_handler->handle_event FOR lo_raiser.

    lo_raiser->raise_event( 'Test Message' ).

      msg = 'Event handling failed.'
    ).

explanation: Dieses Beispiel zeigt, wie abstrakte Klassen für die Implementierung flexibler Event-Handler verwendet werden können. Eine abstrakte Basisklasse definiert die Schnittstelle für die Event-Verarbeitung, während konkrete Unterklassen die spezifische Logik implementieren. Dies ermöglicht eine saubere Trennung von Event-Auslöser und -Verarbeitung.
keywords: ABSTRACT CLASS, EVENTS, Event Handling, Polymorphism

Instructions: Erstellen und füllen Sie eine sortierte interne Tabelle mit Flugdaten (`sflights`) unter Verwendung des `VALUE #` Operators.
hint: Nutzen Sie `VALUE #` und `SORTED TABLE` mit einem eindeutigen Schlüssel.
solution:
CLASS zcl_srt_create_table DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_sflight_data,
             carrid TYPE s_carr_id,
             connid TYPE s_conn_id,
             fldate TYPE s_date,
             price  TYPE s_price,
           END OF ty_sflight_data.
    TYPES: tt_sflight_sorted TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_sflight_data WITH UNIQUE KEY carrid connid.

    METHODS get_sorted_flights RETURNING VALUE(rt_flights) TYPE tt_sflight_sorted.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_srt_create_table IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_sorted_flights.
    SELECT carrid, connid, fldate, price
      FROM sflight
      INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_sflight_raw)
      UP TO 10 ROWS.

    rt_flights = VALUE #( FOR <fs_sflight> IN lt_sflight_raw
                          ( carrid = <fs_sflight>-carrid,
                            connid = <fs_sflight>-connid,
                            fldate = <fs_sflight>-fldate,
                            price  = <fs_sflight>-price ) ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_create_sorted_table FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_create_sorted_table.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_srt_create_table( ).
    DATA(lt_flights) = lo_cut->get_sorted_flights( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_not_initial(
      act = lt_flights,
      msg = 'Sorted table should not be initial.'
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lines( lt_flights ),
      exp = 10,
      msg = 'Expected 10 entries in the sorted table.'
    ).
    DATA(lv_prev_carrid) TYPE s_carr_id.
    DATA(lv_prev_connid) TYPE s_conn_id.
    LOOP AT lt_flights ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_flight>).
      IF sy-tabix > 1.
        cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true(
          act = ( <fs_flight>-carrid > lv_prev_carrid OR
                  ( <fs_flight>-carrid = lv_prev_carrid AND <fs_flight>-connid > lv_prev_connid ) ),
          msg = 'Table is not sorted correctly.'
        ).
      ENDIF.
      lv_prev_carrid = <fs_flight>-carrid.
      lv_prev_connid = <fs_flight>-connid.
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Der `VALUE #` Operator ermöglicht eine deklarative und kompakte Initialisierung von internen Tabellen. In Kombination mit `FOR` Schleifen kann man Daten aus einer Quelle transformieren und direkt in eine sortierte Tabelle einfügen, wobei die Sortierung und Eindeutigkeit durch den Tabellentyp sichergestellt wird.
keywords: SORTED TABLE, VALUE #, Internal Tables, FOR

Instructions: Lesen Sie einen Eintrag aus einer sortierten internen Tabelle mit einem expliziten Schlüssel und dem Tabellen-Ausdruck `itab[ key ... ]`.
hint: Nutzen Sie `itab[ KEY primary_key ... ]` für den schnellen Zugriff.
solution:
CLASS zcl_srt_read_table DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_sflight_data,
             carrid TYPE s_carr_id,
             connid TYPE s_conn_id,
             fldate TYPE s_date,
             price  TYPE s_price,
           END OF ty_sflight_data.
    TYPES: tt_sflight_sorted TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_sflight_data WITH UNIQUE KEY carrid connid.

    METHODS get_flight_details
      IMPORTING
        iv_carrid TYPE s_carr_id
        iv_connid TYPE s_conn_id
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rs_flight) TYPE ty_sflight_data.
  PRIVATE SECTION:
    DATA mt_flights TYPE tt_sflight_sorted.
    METHODS constructor.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_srt_read_table IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
    SELECT carrid, connid, fldate, price
      FROM sflight
      INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_sflight_raw)
      UP TO 100 ROWS.

    mt_flights = VALUE #( FOR <fs_sflight> IN lt_sflight_raw
                          ( carrid = <fs_sflight>-carrid,
                            connid = <fs_sflight>-connid,
                            fldate = <fs_sflight>-fldate,
                            price  = <fs_sflight>-price ) ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD get_flight_details.
    TRY.
        rs_flight = mt_flights[ KEY primary_key carrid = iv_carrid connid = iv_connid ].
      CATCH cx_sy_itab_line_not_found.
        CLEAR rs_flight.
    ENDTRY.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_read_existing_entry FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_read_non_existing_entry FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_read_existing_entry.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_srt_read_table( ).
    DATA(ls_flight) = lo_cut->get_flight_details( iv_carrid = 'LH' iv_connid = '0400' ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_not_initial(
      act = ls_flight-carrid,
      msg = 'Flight details should be found.'
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = ls_flight-carrid,
      exp = 'LH',
      msg = 'Incorrect carrid.'
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = ls_flight-connid,
      exp = '0400',
      msg = 'Incorrect connid.'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD test_read_non_existing_entry.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_srt_read_table( ).
    DATA(ls_flight) = lo_cut->get_flight_details( iv_carrid = 'XX' iv_connid = '9999' ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial(
      act = ls_flight-carrid,
      msg = 'Flight details for non-existing entry should be initial.'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Der Tabellen-Ausdruck `itab[ key ... ]` ermöglicht einen sehr effizienten und lesbaren Zugriff auf Einträge in internen Tabellen, insbesondere bei sortierten Tabellen mit definiertem Schlüssel. Bei sortierten Tabellen wird ein optimierter binärer Suchalgorithmus verwendet, was die Performance erheblich verbessert. Die `TRY...CATCH` Blöcke behandeln den Fall, dass kein Eintrag gefunden wird.
keywords: SORTED TABLE, READ TABLE, Table Expression, KEY, Performance

Instructions: Filtern Sie eine sortierte interne Tabelle nach bestimmten Kriterien unter Verwendung des `FILTER` Ausdrucks.
hint: Nutzen Sie `FILTER #` für deklaratives Filtern.
solution:
CLASS zcl_srt_filter_table DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_sflight_data,
             carrid TYPE s_carr_id,
             connid TYPE s_conn_id,
             fldate TYPE s_date,
             price  TYPE s_price,
           END OF ty_sflight_data.
    TYPES: tt_sflight_sorted TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_sflight_data WITH UNIQUE KEY carrid connid.

    METHODS get_filtered_flights
      IMPORTING
        iv_carrid TYPE s_carr_id
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_filtered_flights) TYPE tt_sflight_sorted.
  PRIVATE SECTION:
    DATA mt_all_flights TYPE tt_sflight_sorted.
    METHODS constructor.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_srt_filter_table IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
    SELECT carrid, connid, fldate, price
      FROM sflight
      INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_sflight_raw)
      UP TO 200 ROWS.

    mt_all_flights = VALUE #( FOR <fs_sflight> IN lt_sflight_raw
                               ( carrid = <fs_sflight>-carrid,
                                 connid = <fs_sflight>-connid,
                                 fldate = <fs_sflight>-fldate,
                                 price  = <fs_sflight>-price ) ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD get_filtered_flights.
    rt_filtered_flights = FILTER #( mt_all_flights WHERE carrid = iv_carrid ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_filter_flights FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_filter_no_results FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_filter_flights.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_srt_filter_table( ).
    DATA(lt_filtered) = lo_cut->get_filtered_flights( 'LH' ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_not_initial(
      act = lt_filtered,
      msg = 'Filtered table for LH should not be initial.'
    ).
    LOOP AT lt_filtered ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_flight>).
      cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
        act = <fs_flight>-carrid,
        exp = 'LH',
        msg = 'Filtered entry has wrong carrid.'
      ).
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD test_filter_no_results.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_srt_filter_table( ).
    DATA(lt_filtered) = lo_cut->get_filtered_flights( 'ZZ' ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial(
      act = lt_filtered,
      msg = 'Filtered table for ZZ should be initial.'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Der `FILTER #` Ausdruck bietet eine moderne und deklarative Möglichkeit, interne Tabellen zu filtern. Er ist besonders effizient bei sortierten Tabellen, da er die vorhandene Sortierung und Schlüsseldefinitionen nutzen kann, um die Suche zu optimieren. Dies führt zu kürzerem, lesbarerem und oft performanterem Code im Vergleich zu traditionellen `LOOP AT WHERE` Konstrukten.
keywords: SORTED TABLE, FILTER #, Internal Tables, Declarative

Instructions: Erstellen Sie eine neue sortierte Tabelle, indem Sie eine bestehende sortierte Tabelle durchlaufen und Einträge modifizieren, unter Verwendung von `FOR` und `VALUE #`.
hint: Nutzen Sie `FOR ... IN ...` und `VALUE #` für die Transformation.
solution:
CLASS zcl_srt_transform_table DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_sflight_data,
             carrid TYPE s_carr_id,
             connid TYPE s_conn_id,
             fldate TYPE s_date,
             price  TYPE s_price,
           END OF ty_sflight_data.
    TYPES: tt_sflight_sorted TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_sflight_data WITH UNIQUE KEY carrid connid.

    METHODS transform_flights
      IMPORTING
        it_source_flights TYPE tt_sflight_sorted
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_transformed_flights) TYPE tt_sflight_sorted.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_srt_transform_table IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD transform_flights.
    rt_transformed_flights = VALUE #( FOR ls_flight IN it_source_flights
                                      ( carrid = ls_flight-carrid,
                                        connid = ls_flight-connid,
                                        fldate = ls_flight-fldate,
                                        price  = ls_flight-price * '1.1' ) ). " Increase price by 10%
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_transform_flights FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_transform_flights.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_sflight_data,
             carrid TYPE s_carr_id,
             connid TYPE s_conn_id,
             fldate TYPE s_date,
             price  TYPE s_price,
           END OF ty_sflight_data.
    TYPES: tt_sflight_sorted TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_sflight_data WITH UNIQUE KEY carrid connid.

    DATA(lt_source) = VALUE tt_sflight_sorted(
      ( carrid = 'LH' connid = '0400' fldate = '20250101' price = '100.00' )
      ( carrid = 'LH' connid = '0401' fldate = '20250102' price = '200.00' )
    ).

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_srt_transform_table( ).
    DATA(lt_transformed) = lo_cut->transform_flights( lt_source ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lines( lt_transformed ),
      exp = 2,
      msg = 'Transformed table should have 2 entries.'
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lt_transformed[ 1 ]-price,
      exp = '110.00',
      msg = 'First flight price not transformed correctly.'
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lt_transformed[ 2 ]-price,
      exp = '220.00',
      msg = 'Second flight price not transformed correctly.'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Die Kombination aus `FOR ... IN ...` und `VALUE #` ist eine sehr mächtige und moderne Art, interne Tabellen zu transformieren. Sie ermöglicht es, eine neue Tabelle zu erstellen, indem man über eine bestehende iteriert und dabei die einzelnen Zeilen modifiziert oder neue Zeilen basierend auf der Logik erzeugt. Dies ist deklarativer und oft performanter als traditionelle `LOOP AT ... APPEND` oder `LOOP AT ... MODIFY` Konstrukte.
keywords: SORTED TABLE, FOR, VALUE #, Internal Tables, Transformation

Instructions: Gruppieren Sie Einträge in einer sortierten Tabelle nach einem Schlüssel und aggregieren Sie Daten innerhalb jeder Gruppe unter Verwendung von `LOOP AT ... GROUP BY`.
hint: Nutzen Sie `LOOP AT ... GROUP BY ...` mit `REDUCE` oder `SUM` für die Aggregation.
solution:
CLASS zcl_srt_group_table DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_sflight_data,
             carrid TYPE s_carr_id,
             connid TYPE s_conn_id,
             fldate TYPE s_date,
             price  TYPE s_price,
           END OF ty_sflight_data.
    TYPES: tt_sflight_sorted TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_sflight_data WITH UNIQUE KEY carrid connid.

    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_grouped_result,
             carrid    TYPE s_carr_id,
             total_price TYPE s_price,
             flight_count TYPE i,
           END OF ty_grouped_result.
    TYPES: tt_grouped_result TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_grouped_result WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS group_flights_by_carrier
      IMPORTING
        it_flights TYPE tt_sflight_sorted
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_grouped_data) TYPE tt_grouped_result.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_srt_group_table IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD group_flights_by_carrier.
    LOOP AT it_flights INTO DATA(ls_flight) GROUP BY ls_flight-carrid ASCENDING
                                             INTO DATA(ls_group_key).
      DATA(lv_total_price) = REDUCE s_price(
        INIT sum = '0.00'
        FOR <fs_group_member> IN GROUP ls_flight
        NEXT sum = sum + <fs_group_member>-price
      ).
      DATA(lv_flight_count) = REDUCE i(
        INIT count = 0
        FOR <fs_group_member> IN GROUP ls_flight
        NEXT count = count + 1
      ).

      APPEND VALUE ty_grouped_result(
        carrid     = ls_group_key-carrid
        total_price = lv_total_price
        flight_count = lv_flight_count

Instructions: Verwenden Sie den `REDUCE` Operator, um den Gesamtpreis aller Flüge in einer sortierten Tabelle zu berechnen.
hint: Nutzen Sie `REDUCE` mit einer `INIT` Variablen und `FOR` Schleife.
solution:
CLASS zcl_srt_reduce_table DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_sflight_data,
             carrid TYPE s_carr_id,
             connid TYPE s_conn_id,
             fldate TYPE s_date,
             price  TYPE s_price,
           END OF ty_sflight_data.
    TYPES: tt_sflight_sorted TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_sflight_data WITH UNIQUE KEY carrid connid.

    METHODS calculate_total_price
      IMPORTING
        it_flights TYPE tt_sflight_sorted
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_total_price) TYPE s_price.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_srt_reduce_table IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD calculate_total_price.
    rv_total_price = REDUCE s_price(
      INIT sum_price = '0.00'
      FOR ls_flight IN it_flights
      NEXT sum_price = sum_price + ls_flight-price
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

Er ist sehr ausdrucksstark und macht den Code kürzer und lesbarer als traditionelle `LOOP AT ... ENDLOOP` mit manueller Akkumulation. Die `INIT` Klausel setzt den Startwert für die Reduktion.

Instructions: Erstellen Sie eine sortierte Tabelle mit doppelten Einträgen und entfernen Sie Duplikate effizient unter Beibehaltung der Sortierung.
hint: Nutzen Sie `DELETE ADJACENT DUPLICATES` oder eine `SORTED TABLE` mit `UNIQUE KEY`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_srt_deduplicate DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_data,
             key_field TYPE string,
             value_field TYPE string,
           END OF ty_data.
    TYPES: tt_data_sorted TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_data WITH NON-UNIQUE KEY key_field.
    TYPES: tt_data_unique TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_data WITH UNIQUE KEY key_field.

    METHODS remove_duplicates
      IMPORTING
        it_source TYPE tt_data_sorted
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_unique) TYPE tt_data_unique.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_srt_deduplicate IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD remove_duplicates.
    " The most efficient way to get unique entries from a sorted table
    " is to assign it to a sorted table with a UNIQUE KEY.
    rt_unique = it_source.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_remove_duplicates.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_data,
             key_field TYPE string,
             value_field TYPE string,
           END OF ty_data.
    TYPES: tt_data_sorted TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_data WITH NON-UNIQUE KEY key_field.

    DATA(lt_source) = VALUE tt_data_sorted(
      ( key_field = 'A' value_field = 'Val1' )
      ( key_field = 'A' value_field = 'Val2' )
      ( key_field = 'B' value_field = 'Val3' )
      ( key_field = 'C' value_field = 'Val4' )
      ( key_field = 'C' value_field = 'Val5' )
    ).

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_srt_deduplicate( ).
    DATA(lt_unique) = lo_cut->remove_duplicates( lt_source ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lines( lt_unique ),
      exp = 3,
      msg = 'Expected 3 unique entries.'
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_unique[ 1 ]-key_field, exp = 'A' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_unique[ 2 ]-key_field, exp = 'B' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_unique[ 3 ]-key_field, exp = 'C' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_unique[ 1 ]-value_field, exp = 'Val1' ). " First occurrence is kept
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD test_no_duplicates.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_data,
             key_field TYPE string,
             value_field TYPE string,
           END OF ty_data.
    TYPES: tt_data_sorted TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_data WITH NON-UNIQUE KEY key_field.

    DATA(lt_source) = VALUE tt_data_sorted(
      ( key_field = 'X' value_field = 'ValX' )
      ( key_field = 'Y' value_field = 'ValY' )
    ).

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_srt_deduplicate( ).
    DATA(lt_unique) = lo_cut->remove_duplicates( lt_source ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lines( lt_unique ),
      exp = 2,
      msg = 'Expected 2 entries (no duplicates).' 
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD test_empty_table.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_data,
             key_field TYPE string,
             value_field TYPE string,
           END OF ty_data.
    TYPES: tt_data_sorted TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_data WITH NON-UNIQUE KEY key_field.

    DATA(lt_source) = VALUE tt_data_sorted( ).

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_srt_deduplicate( ).
    DATA(lt_unique) = lo_cut->remove_duplicates( lt_source ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial(
      act = lt_unique,
      msg = 'Expected empty table for empty input.'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Das Zuweisen einer sortierten Tabelle (mit nicht-eindeutigem Schlüssel) zu einer sortierten Tabelle mit einem `UNIQUE KEY` ist die modernste und effizienteste Methode, um Duplikate zu entfernen, während die Sortierung beibehalten wird. Das System entfernt automatisch alle Duplikate basierend auf dem eindeutigen Schlüssel und behält dabei die erste gefundene Zeile bei. Dies ist performanter und kürzer als `DELETE ADJACENT DUPLICATES`.
keywords: SORTED TABLE, UNIQUE KEY, Duplicates, Assignment, Performance

Instructions: Führen Sie eine innere Verknüpfung (INNER JOIN) zwischen zwei sortierten internen Tabellen durch, um passende Einträge zu finden.
hint: Nutzen Sie `FOR ... IN ... WHERE ...` mit `VALUE #` für die Verknüpfung.
solution:
CLASS zcl_srt_inner_join DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_table1_data,
             id TYPE i,
             value1 TYPE string,
           END OF ty_table1_data.
    TYPES: tt_table1_sorted TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_table1_data WITH UNIQUE KEY id.

    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_table2_data,
             id TYPE i,
             value2 TYPE string,
           END OF ty_table2_data.
    TYPES: tt_table2_sorted TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_table2_data WITH UNIQUE KEY id.

    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_joined_result,
             id TYPE i,
             value1 TYPE string,
             value2 TYPE string,
           END OF ty_joined_result.
    TYPES: tt_joined_result TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_joined_result WITH UNIQUE KEY id.

    METHODS perform_inner_join
      IMPORTING
        it_table1 TYPE tt_table1_sorted
        it_table2 TYPE tt_table2_sorted
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_joined) TYPE tt_joined_result.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_srt_inner_join IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD perform_inner_join.
    rt_joined = VALUE #( FOR ls_t1 IN it_table1
                           FOR ls_t2 IN it_table2 WHERE ( ls_t2-id = ls_t1-id )
                           ( id = ls_t1-id,
                             value1 = ls_t1-value1,
                             value2 = ls_t2-value2 ) ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

  METHOD test_inner_join.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_table1_data,

    TYPES: tt_table2_sorted TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_table2_data WITH UNIQUE KEY id.

    DATA(lt_table1) = VALUE tt_table1_sorted(
      ( id = 1 value1 = 'A' )
      ( id = 2 value1 = 'B' )
      ( id = 3 value1 = 'C' )
    ).

    DATA(lt_table2) = VALUE tt_table2_sorted(
      ( id = 2 value2 = 'X' )
      ( id = 3 value2 = 'Y' )
      ( id = 4 value2 = 'Z' )
    ).

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_srt_inner_join( ).
    DATA(lt_joined) = lo_cut->perform_inner_join( it_table1 = lt_table1 it_table2 = lt_table2 ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lines( lt_joined ),
      exp = 2,
      msg = 'Expected 2 joined entries.'
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_joined[ 1 ]-id, exp = 2 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_joined[ 1 ]-value1, exp = 'B' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_joined[ 1 ]-value2, exp = 'X' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_joined[ 2 ]-id, exp = 3 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_joined[ 2 ]-value1, exp = 'C' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_joined[ 2 ]-value2, exp = 'Y' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD test_inner_join_no_match.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_table1_data,
             id TYPE i,
             value1 TYPE string,
           END OF ty_table1_data.
    TYPES: tt_table1_sorted TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_table1_data WITH UNIQUE KEY id.

    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_table2_data,
             id TYPE i,
             value2 TYPE string,
           END OF ty_table2_data.
    TYPES: tt_table2_sorted TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_table2_data WITH UNIQUE KEY id.

    DATA(lt_table1) = VALUE tt_table1_sorted(
      ( id = 1 value1 = 'A' )
    ).

    DATA(lt_table2) = VALUE tt_table2_sorted(
      ( id = 2 value2 = 'X' )
    ).

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_srt_inner_join( ).
    DATA(lt_joined) = lo_cut->perform_inner_join( it_table1 = lt_table1 it_table2 = lt_table2 ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial(
      act = lt_joined,
      msg = 'Expected empty table for no matching entries.'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD test_inner_join_empty_table.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_table1_data,
             id TYPE i,
             value1 TYPE string,
           END OF ty_table1_data.
    TYPES: tt_table1_sorted TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_table1_data WITH UNIQUE KEY id.

    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_table2_data,
             id TYPE i,
             value2 TYPE string,
           END OF ty_table2_data.
    TYPES: tt_table2_sorted TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_table2_data WITH UNIQUE KEY id.

    DATA(lt_table1) = VALUE tt_table1_sorted(
      ( id = 1 value1 = 'A' )
    ).

    DATA(lt_table2) = VALUE tt_table2_sorted( ).

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_srt_inner_join( ).
    DATA(lt_joined) = lo_cut->perform_inner_join( it_table1 = lt_table1 it_table2 = lt_table2 ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial(
      act = lt_joined,
      msg = 'Expected empty table when one input table is empty.'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Die Kombination von `FOR ... IN ...` mit einer verschachtelten `FOR ... IN ... WHERE ...` Schleife und dem `VALUE #` Operator ermöglicht eine deklarative und effiziente Implementierung von Joins zwischen internen Tabellen. Bei sortierten Tabellen kann die `WHERE` Bedingung für die innere Schleife sehr performant sein, da sie die Sortierung und Schlüsseldefinitionen nutzen kann, um schnell passende Einträge zu finden.
keywords: SORTED TABLE, INNER JOIN, FOR, VALUE #, Internal Tables

Instructions: Erstellen Sie eine sortierte Tabelle und verwenden Sie den `CORRESPONDING` Operator, um Daten aus einer anderen Struktur oder Tabelle zuzuweisen.
hint: Nutzen Sie `CORRESPONDING #` für die feldnamenbasierte Zuweisung.
solution:
CLASS zcl_srt_corresponding DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_source_data,
             carrid TYPE s_carr_id,
             connid TYPE s_conn_id,
             fldate TYPE s_date,
             price  TYPE s_price,
             currency TYPE s_curr,
           END OF ty_source_data.
    TYPES: tt_source_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_source_data WITH EMPTY KEY.

    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_target_data,
             carrid TYPE s_carr_id,
             connid TYPE s_conn_id,
             price  TYPE s_price,
             destination TYPE string,
           END OF ty_target_data.
    TYPES: tt_target_sorted TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_target_data WITH UNIQUE KEY carrid connid.

    METHODS map_data_to_sorted_table
      IMPORTING
        it_source TYPE tt_source_data
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_target) TYPE tt_target_sorted.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_srt_corresponding IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD map_data_to_sorted_table.
    rt_target = CORRESPONDING #( it_source MAPPING destination = 'N/A' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

explanation: Der `CORRESPONDING #` Operator ermöglicht eine feldnamenbasierte Zuweisung von Daten zwischen Strukturen oder internen Tabellen. Er ist besonders nützlich, wenn Quell- und Zielstrukturen ähnliche Feldnamen haben, aber nicht identisch sind. Mit der `MAPPING` Klausel können Felder umbenannt oder mit Konstanten belegt werden. Bei der Zuweisung zu einer sortierten Tabelle wird die Sortierung automatisch beibehalten.

Instructions: Deserialisieren Sie einen potenziell fehlerhaften JSON-String und fangen Sie dabei auftretende Ausnahmen ab.
hint: Verwenden Sie `TRY...CATCH` für `cx_fdt_json_error`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_json_error_handler DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_data,
             field1 TYPE string,
             field2 TYPE i,
           END OF ty_data.
    TYPES tt_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_data WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS deserialize_with_error_handling
      IMPORTING
        iv_json TYPE string
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_data) TYPE tt_data
      RAISING
        cx_fdt_json_error.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_json_error_handler IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD deserialize_with_error_handling.
    TRY.
        DATA(lo_json_reader) = cl_fdt_json=>create_data_from_json( iv_json ).
        lo_json_reader->get_data( CHANGING c_data = rt_data ).
      CATCH cx_fdt_json_error INTO DATA(lx_json_error).
        " Log error or re-raise with custom message
        RAISE EXCEPTION NEW cx_fdt_json_error( textid = lx_json_error->textid previous = lx_json_error ).
    ENDTRY.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_deserialize_valid FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_deserialize_invalid RAISING cx_fdt_json_error FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_deserialize_valid.
    DATA(lv_json) = `[{"FIELD1":"Test","FIELD2":123}]`.
    DATA(lo_handler) = NEW zcl_json_error_handler( ).
    DATA(lt_data) = lo_handler->deserialize_with_error_handling( lv_json ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lines( lt_data ) exp = 1 ).
    READ TABLE lt_data INDEX 1 INTO DATA(ls_data).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = ls_data-field1 exp = 'Test' ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_deserialize_invalid.
    DATA(lv_json_invalid) = `{"FIELD1":"Test","FIELD2":abc}`. " Invalid JSON
    DATA(lo_handler) = NEW zcl_json_error_handler( ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>expect_exception(
      EXPORTING
        i_exception_class = 'CX_FDT_JSON_ERROR'
        i_method          = lo_handler->deserialize_with_error_handling
        i_parameter_list  = VALUE #( ( name = 'IV_JSON' value = lv_json_invalid ) )
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Die explizite Fehlerbehandlung mit `TRY...CATCH` für `cx_fdt_json_error` ist entscheidend für robuste Anwendungen, die mit externen JSON-Daten interagieren.
keywords: JSON, Error Handling, Exception, cl_fdt_json

solution:
CLASS zcl_abapedit_add_comment DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS add_comment_to_code
      IMPORTING
        iv_original_code TYPE string
        iv_comment_text  TYPE string
        io_container TYPE REF TO cl_gui_container OPTIONAL " For actual GUI usage
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_updated_code) TYPE string.

  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA mo_editor TYPE REF TO cl_gui_abapedit.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_abapedit_add_comment IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD add_comment_to_code.
    IF io_container IS SUPPLIED.
      CREATE OBJECT mo_editor
        EXPORTING
          parent = io_container.
    ELSE.
      CREATE OBJECT mo_editor.
    ENDIF.

    mo_editor->set_text_as_stream( iv_original_code ).

    DATA(lv_comment_block) = |* { iv_comment_text }{ cl_abap_char_utilities=>cr_lf }|.
    DATA(lv_new_code) = lv_comment_block && iv_original_code.

    mo_editor->set_text_as_stream( lv_new_code ).
    mo_editor->get_text_as_stream( IMPORTING text = rv_updated_code ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

Instructions: Löschen Sie den gesamten Inhalt eines `cl_gui_abapedit`-Kontrollelements.
hint: Verwenden Sie die Methode `set_text_as_stream` mit einem leeren String.
solution:
CLASS zcl_abapedit_clear_content DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS clear_editor_content
      IMPORTING
        io_container TYPE REF TO cl_gui_container OPTIONAL " For actual GUI usage
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_is_empty) TYPE abap_bool.

    METHODS set_initial_content
      IMPORTING
        iv_code TYPE string
        io_container TYPE REF TO cl_gui_container OPTIONAL.

  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA mo_editor TYPE REF TO cl_gui_abapedit.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_abapedit_clear_content IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD set_initial_content.
    IF io_container IS SUPPLIED.
      CREATE OBJECT mo_editor
        EXPORTING
          parent = io_container.
    ELSE.
      CREATE OBJECT mo_editor.
    ENDIF.
    mo_editor->set_text_as_stream( iv_code ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD clear_editor_content.
    IF mo_editor IS BOUND.
      mo_editor->set_text_as_stream( '' ).
      DATA(lv_current_content) TYPE string.
      mo_editor->get_text_as_stream( IMPORTING text = lv_current_content ).
      rv_is_empty = COND #( WHEN lv_current_content IS INITIAL THEN abap_true ELSE abap_false ).
    ELSE.
      rv_is_empty = abap_true. " Editor not created, so content is effectively empty
    ENDIF.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.

    METHODS test_clear_content FOR TESTING.

Instructions: Führen Sie eine Suche nach einem bestimmten Text im `cl_gui_abapedit`-Kontrollelement durch und markieren Sie die Fundstellen.
hint: Verwenden Sie Methoden wie `find_next` und `set_selection_pos`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_abapedit_search DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS search_and_select
      IMPORTING
        iv_code TYPE string
        iv_search_term TYPE string
        io_container TYPE REF TO cl_gui_container OPTIONAL " For actual GUI usage
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_found_count) TYPE i.

  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA mo_editor TYPE REF TO cl_gui_abapedit.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_abapedit_search IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD search_and_select.
    DATA: lv_offset TYPE i,
          lv_length TYPE i,
          lv_line   TYPE i.

    IF io_container IS SUPPLIED.
      CREATE OBJECT mo_editor
        EXPORTING
          parent = io_container.
    ELSE.
      CREATE OBJECT mo_editor.
    ENDIF.

    mo_editor->set_text_as_stream( iv_code ).
    mo_editor->set_selection_pos( row = 1 col = 1 ). " Start search from beginning

    DO.
      TRY.
          mo_editor->find_next(
            EXPORTING
              string = iv_search_term
              case_sensitive = abap_false
            IMPORTING
              offset = lv_offset
              length = lv_length
              line   = lv_line
          ).
          rv_found_count = rv_found_count + 1.
          " In a real GUI, you would now highlight or scroll to the position.
          " For this example, we just count.
          " mo_editor->set_selection_pos( row = lv_line col = lv_offset + 1 length = lv_length ).
        CATCH cx_gui_error.
          EXIT.
      ENDTRY.
    ENDDO.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_search_and_select FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_search_and_select.
    DATA(lv_code) = `REPORT z_test.
WRITE 'Hello'.
WRITE 'World'.
WRITE 'Hello again'.`.
    DATA(lv_search) = 'Hello'.
    DATA(lo_editor_wrapper) = NEW zcl_abapedit_search( ).

    DATA(lv_found_count) = lo_editor_wrapper->search_and_select( 
      iv_code = lv_code 
      iv_search_term = lv_search 
    ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( msg = 'Sollte 2 Fundstellen haben' act = lv_found_count exp = 2 ).

    DATA(lv_search_not_found) = 'NonExistent'.
    DATA(lv_found_count_none) = lo_editor_wrapper->search_and_select( 
      iv_code = lv_code 
      iv_search_term = lv_search_not_found 
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( msg = 'Sollte 0 Fundstellen haben' act = lv_found_count_none exp = 0 ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Die Suchfunktionalität im `cl_gui_abapedit` ermöglicht es, Textmuster im Code zu finden. Obwohl das tatsächliche Hervorheben eine GUI-Interaktion erfordert, zeigt dieses Beispiel die Logik zum Auffinden aller Vorkommen eines Suchbegriffs. Die Verwendung von `TRY...CATCH` für `cx_gui_error` ist hier wichtig, da `find_next` eine Exception wirft, wenn kein weiteres Vorkommen gefunden wird.

CLASS zcl_url_extractor DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.

      IMPORTING
        iv_text TYPE string
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_urls) TYPE string_table
      RAISING
        cx_abap_regex_error.

CLASS zcl_url_extractor IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD extract_urls.
    DATA(lv_pattern) = `https?://[a-zA-Z0-9./-]+`.
    DATA(lo_regex) = NEW cl_abap_regex( pattern = lv_pattern case_sensitive = abap_false ).
    DATA(lo_matcher) = lo_regex->create_matcher( text = iv_text ).

    DATA(lt_matches) = lo_matcher->find_all( ).

    LOOP AT lt_matches INTO DATA(ls_match).
      APPEND ls_match-submatch TO rt_urls.
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDMETHOD.

Instructions: Teilen Sie einen String anhand eines komplexen Delimiters, der entweder ' UND ' oder ' ODER ' (Groß-/Kleinschreibung ignorierend) sein kann, und geben Sie die einzelnen Teile in einer Tabelle zurück.
hint: Verwenden Sie `cl_abap_regex` mit der Option `case_sensitive = abap_false` und iterieren Sie über die gefundenen Delimiter, um den String manuell zu teilen.
solution:
CLASS zcl_complex_splitter DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS split_by_complex_delimiter
      IMPORTING
        iv_text TYPE string
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_parts) TYPE string_table
      RAISING
        cx_abap_regex_error.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_complex_splitter IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD split_by_complex_delimiter.
    DATA(lv_pattern) = `\s+(UND|ODER)\s+`.
    DATA(lo_regex) = NEW cl_abap_regex( pattern = lv_pattern case_sensitive = abap_false ).
    DATA(lo_matcher) = lo_regex->create_matcher( text = iv_text ).

    DATA(lt_matches) = lo_matcher->find_all( ).
    DATA(lv_last_offset) = 0.

    IF lt_matches IS INITIAL.
      APPEND iv_text TO rt_parts.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    LOOP AT lt_matches INTO DATA(ls_match).
      APPEND substring( val = iv_text off = lv_last_offset len = ls_match-offset - lv_last_offset ) TO rt_parts.
      lv_last_offset = ls_match-offset + ls_match-length.
    ENDLOOP.

    APPEND substring( val = iv_text off = lv_last_offset ) TO rt_parts.

    " Remove empty parts that might result from leading/trailing delimiters
    DELETE rt_parts WHERE table_line IS INITIAL.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

  PRIVATE SECTION:

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_split_und_oder.
    DATA(lo_splitter) = NEW zcl_complex_splitter( ).

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_split_mixed_case.
    DATA(lo_splitter) = NEW zcl_complex_splitter( ).
    DATA(lv_input) = `Rot und Blau oder Gruen`.
    DATA(lt_expected) = VALUE string_table( ( 'Rot' ) ( 'Blau' ) ( 'Gruen' ) ).
    DATA(lt_actual) = lo_splitter->split_by_complex_delimiter( lv_input ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_actual exp = lt_expected ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_no_delimiter.
    DATA(lo_splitter) = NEW zcl_complex_splitter( ).
    DATA(lv_input) = `Ein einfacher Satz`.
    DATA(lt_expected) = VALUE string_table( ( 'Ein einfacher Satz' ) ).
    DATA(lt_actual) = lo_splitter->split_by_complex_delimiter( lv_input ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_actual exp = lt_expected ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_leading_trailing_delimiter.
    DATA(lo_splitter) = NEW zcl_complex_splitter( ).
    DATA(lv_input) = ` UND Teil1 ODER Teil2 UND `.
    DATA(lt_expected) = VALUE string_table( ( 'Teil1' ) ( 'Teil2' ) ).
    DATA(lt_actual) = lo_splitter->split_by_complex_delimiter( lv_input ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_actual exp = lt_expected ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Dieses Beispiel zeigt, wie man einen String anhand eines komplexen, regulären Ausdrucks teilt, der mehrere Delimiter und Groß-/Kleinschreibung ignorieren kann. Da ABAP keine direkte 'split by regex'-Funktion wie in anderen Sprachen bietet, wird dies durch das Finden aller Delimiter mit `find_all` und anschließendes manuelles Extrahieren der Substrings realisiert. Dies ist eine flexible und leistungsstarke Methode für fortgeschrittene String-Manipulationen.
keywords: REGEX, SPLIT, Delimiter, String, cl_abap_regex, cl_abap_matcher, find_all

Instructions: Erstellen Sie dynamisch eine interne Tabelle mit den Feldern 'ID' (Typ I) und 'Beschreibung' (Typ String), füllen Sie diese mit drei Datensätzen und zeigen Sie sie in einem ALV an.
hint: Verwenden Sie `cl_alv_table_create=>create_dynamic_table` zur Erstellung der Tabelle und `cl_salv_table=>factory` zur ALV-Anzeige.
solution:
CLASS zcl_dynamic_alv_basic DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS display_dynamic_alv.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_dynamic_alv_basic IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD display_dynamic_alv.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_field_cat,
             fieldname TYPE fieldname,
             inttype   TYPE inttype,
             intlen    TYPE intlen,
             decimals  TYPE decimals,
             coltext   TYPE lvc_coltext,
           END OF ty_field_cat.

    DATA: lt_field_cat TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_field_cat,
          lr_table     TYPE REF TO data,
          lr_struct_descr TYPE REF TO cl_abap_structdescr,
          lr_data_descr   TYPE REF TO cl_abap_elemdescr.

    " Define field catalog
    APPEND VALUE #( fieldname = 'ID' inttype = 'I' intlen = 4 coltext = 'Identifikator' ) TO lt_field_cat.
    APPEND VALUE #( fieldname = 'DESCRIPTION' inttype = 'C' intlen = 100 coltext = 'Beschreibung' ) TO lt_field_cat.

    " Create dynamic table
    cl_alv_table_create=>create_dynamic_table(
      EXPORTING
        it_fieldcatalog = lt_field_cat
      IMPORTING
        ep_table        = lr_table
    ).

    FIELD-SYMBOLS: <lt_dynamic_table> TYPE STANDARD TABLE,
                   <ls_dynamic_line>  TYPE any.

    ASSIGN lr_table->* TO <lt_dynamic_table>.

    " Get structure description for dynamic line creation
    lr_struct_descr ?= cl_abap_typedescr=>describe_by_data( <lt_dynamic_table> ).

    " Fill dynamic table
    CREATE DATA <ls_dynamic_line> TYPE HANDLE lr_struct_descr.
    ASSIGN <ls_dynamic_line> TO <ls_dynamic_line>.

    ASSIGN COMPONENT 'ID' OF STRUCTURE <ls_dynamic_line> TO FIELD-SYMBOL(<lv_id>).
    ASSIGN COMPONENT 'DESCRIPTION' OF STRUCTURE <ls_dynamic_line> TO FIELD-SYMBOL(<lv_desc>).

    IF <lv_id> IS ASSIGNED AND <lv_desc> IS ASSIGNED.
      <lv_id> = 1.
      <lv_desc> = 'Erster Eintrag'.
      APPEND <ls_dynamic_line> TO <lt_dynamic_table>.

      <lv_id> = 2.
      <lv_desc> = 'Zweiter Eintrag'.
      APPEND <ls_dynamic_line> TO <lt_dynamic_table>.

      <lv_id> = 3.
      <lv_desc> = 'Dritter Eintrag'.
      APPEND <ls_dynamic_line> TO <lt_dynamic_table>.
    ENDIF.

    " Display ALV
    TRY.
        cl_salv_table=>factory(
          IMPORTING
            r_salv_table = DATA(lo_salv_table)
          CHANGING
            t_table      = <lt_dynamic_table>
        ).
        lo_salv_table->display( ).
      CATCH cx_salv_msg.
        " Handle error
    ENDTRY.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

hint: Fügen Sie dem Feldkatalog eine neue Spalte hinzu und füllen Sie diese manuell nach dem SELECT durch Iteration über die dynamische Tabelle.

CLASS zcl_alv_calculated_field DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.

CLASS zcl_alv_calculated_field IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD display_calculated_alv.
    DATA: lt_field_cat TYPE lvc_t_fcat,
          lr_table     TYPE REF TO data.

    CONSTANTS: lc_currency_rate TYPE f VALUE '1.2'.

    " Define field catalog for SFLIGHTS fields + calculated field
    APPEND VALUE #( fieldname = 'CARRID'   coltext = 'Fluggesellschaft' ) TO lt_field_cat.
    APPEND VALUE #( fieldname = 'CONNID'   coltext = 'Flugnummer' ) TO lt_field_cat.
    APPEND VALUE #( fieldname = 'FLDATE'   coltext = 'Flugdatum' ) TO lt_field_cat.
    APPEND VALUE #( fieldname = 'PRICE'    coltext = 'Preis' ) TO lt_field_cat.
    APPEND VALUE #( fieldname = 'CURRENCY' coltext = 'Währung' ) TO lt_field_cat.
    APPEND VALUE #( fieldname = 'TOTAL_AMOUNT' datatype = 'DEC' intlen = 15 decimals = 2 coltext = 'Gesamtbetrag' ) TO lt_field_cat.

    " Create dynamic table
    cl_alv_table_create=>create_dynamic_table(
      EXPORTING
        it_fieldcatalog = lt_field_cat
      IMPORTING
        ep_table        = lr_table
    ).

    FIELD-SYMBOLS: <lt_dynamic_sflights> TYPE STANDARD TABLE,
                   <ls_dynamic_line>  TYPE any.

    ASSIGN lr_table->* TO <lt_dynamic_sflights>.

    " Select data into the dynamic table (excluding TOTAL_AMOUNT for now)
    SELECT carrid, connid, fldate, price, currency
      FROM sflights
      INTO CORRESPONDING FIELDS OF TABLE <lt_dynamic_sflights>
      UP TO 100 ROWS.

    " Calculate and fill TOTAL_AMOUNT
    LOOP AT <lt_dynamic_sflights> ASSIGNING <ls_dynamic_line>.
      ASSIGN COMPONENT 'PRICE' OF STRUCTURE <ls_dynamic_line> TO FIELD-SYMBOL(<lv_price>).
      ASSIGN COMPONENT 'TOTAL_AMOUNT' OF STRUCTURE <ls_dynamic_line> TO FIELD-SYMBOL(<lv_total_amount>).

      IF <lv_price> IS ASSIGNED AND <lv_total_amount> IS ASSIGNED.
        <lv_total_amount> = <lv_price> * lc_currency_rate.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.

    " Display ALV
    TRY.
        cl_salv_table=>factory(
          IMPORTING
            r_salv_table = DATA(lo_salv_table)
          CHANGING
            t_table      = <lt_dynamic_sflights>
        ).
        lo_salv_table->display( ).
      CATCH cx_salv_msg.
        " Handle error
    ENDTRY.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
